text:
**My pick: Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA for most people, with standard Eneloop or IKEA LADDA as cheaper alternatives.**

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA**
- It is rated at about 2,550 mAh, keeps about 85% charge after a year, and is good for roughly 500 recharges. Digital Camera World's reviewer has used it for years in flash testing and reports no reliability problems ([Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)).
- The tradeoffs are fewer recharge cycles and a higher price (listed around $22-$35 for a 4-pack).
- Where to buy: the Amazon, Adorama and Newegg links are on [this guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries). I wasn't given direct product URLs.

**Best for longevity: Panasonic Eneloop (standard)**
- It has lower capacity (2,000 mAh), but it is rated for about 2,100 recharges and holds 70% charge after 10 years. It suits remotes, controllers, and anything you recharge often ([Digital Camera World](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries)).

**Best value if you're near an IKEA: LADDA**
- Charge-Test's lab measurements found the LADDA 2450 mAh averaged about 2,450 mAh at low load and 2,348 mAh at 1A, close to Eneloop Pro. They conclude it is Eneloop-class at a lower price, though IKEA has never confirmed who makes it ([Charge-Test](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/)).
- IKEA's US page currently lists only the **1900 mAh version at $9.99 for 4**. Buy it [here](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/). The $7.99 price for the 2450 mAh pack in some reviews appears to be a European price, so check your local store for that one.

**Best for bulk: Tenergy Premium PRO 2,800 mAh**
- It comes in a 20-pack for $42.99, with 4-packs at $11.99. The seller claims 85% charge after a year and 1,200 cycles. These are the seller's own figures, and I found no independent tests ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries-2026-tests-capacity-self-discharge-panasonic-enel)). Buy it [here](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack) (affiliate link).
- If you need a charger, the [Tenergy TN480U 8-bay](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger) is $23.99, though it doesn't include a power adapter.

**Things to know**
- **Voltage:** NiMH cells are 1.2V, not 1.5V like alkalines. A few voltage-sensitive devices may read them as low. Digital Camera World lists the EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA as a fix, but I have no test data on it.
- **Capacity claims:** I'd be wary of the Frame & Focal articles. Their figures don't match the manufacturer specs or each other, for example Eneloop Pro at 2,100 mAh versus its 2,550 mAh rating. I didn't rely on them. Likewise, the sources disagree on the cycle life of Amazon Basics cells, so I wouldn't pick those on the strength of this research.
- **Which to choose:** For high-drain devices like cameras, flashes and flashlights, get Eneloop Pro or LADDA 2450. For everyday household use, standard Eneloop or LADDA 1900 is enough.
